title: Makefile builds the debug XCFramework while the app target requires the release XCFramework

evidence.quote:
generate: $(XCFRAMEWORK_DIR)

tuist generate

build: $(XCFRAMEWORK_DIR)

tuist build

reasoning: The top-level release/build entrypoints only ensure the debug XCFramework exists, but the Tuist app target references the release XCFramework. On a clean checkout, `make generate` or `make build` can successfully build `../shared/build/XCFrameworks/debug/EpilogueShared.xcframework` and then fail during project generation/build because `../shared/build/XCFrameworks/release/EpilogueShared.xcframework` is still missing. This is especially risky for release packaging because the automation gives a false prerequisite and can leave CI or local release builds depending on stale release artifacts.
reproduction: From a clean tree, remove `../shared/build/XCFrameworks`, then run `make build`. The Makefile prerequisite creates/checks the debug path, while Tuist resolves the release path declared in `App/Project.swift`.
recommendation: Align the Makefile prerequisite with the path used by Tuist. Either set `XCFRAMEWORK_DIR` to `../shared/build/XCFrameworks/release/EpilogueShared.xcframework` and invoke the release KMP XCFramework task, or update the Tuist dependency to match the artifact intentionally produced for the build configuration.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or release validation commands exercise a clean checkout `make build`/`make generate` path with the XCFramework directory absent.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI release packaging smoke test that deletes `../shared/build/XCFrameworks`, runs the intended Makefile build/generate target, and verifies the XCFramework path referenced by Tuist exists before `tuist generate`.
minimumFixScope: Makefile XCFramework path/task and, if needed, the matching Tuist XCFramework dependency path.
